paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot displays the empirical generalization errors (labeled as "Errors (RTE)") for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B, across different hidden dimensions, which are represented on the x-axis as "Rank" with values 4, 16, 64, and 256 on a logarithmic scale. The y-axis, labeled "Errors (RTE)", ranges from 0.3 to 0.9 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. The data is presented as a single black line connecting green circular markers at each rank, with vertical error bars indicating variability. At Rank 4, the error is approximately 0.35; at Rank 16, it remains nearly constant at around 0.33; at Rank 64, the error increases to about 0.4; and at Rank 256, it rises further to approximately 0.65. The trend shows that smaller ranks (i.e., smaller adapters) achieve lower generalization errors, with the error increasing as the rank increases.
